h: A Riverside Route From Gamebox to Tate Modern
p: Because you'll be in a private room, it's worth thinking about who's coming and what kind of game suits them. Gamebox has a selection of themes, some aimed squarely at families with young children and others designed for older players who want something faster and more frantic. Check what's available when booking, and let everyone have a say in the choice.

One of the best things about this location is how easily it fits into a stroll along the river. Here's a simple route that works well. Start with your Gamebox session, then head east along the riverside walk past the Southbank Centre and the National Theatre. Under Waterloo Bridge you'll find the outdoor second-hand book market, and on the other side BFI Southbank, home of the British Film Institute, with its café and riverside tables.

Keep walking and you'll pass Gabriel's Wharf, a quirky little cluster of independent shops and places to eat, and then the Oxo Tower, with its famous windows spelling out the old brand name. Keep going a little further and you'll reach Tate Modern, the huge art gallery in the former Bankside Power Station, which is free to enter and has a viewing level with great views over the city. The Millennium Bridge right outside will take you across the Thames to St Paul's Cathedral.

Along the way, look out for the skateboarders in the Undercroft beneath the Southbank Centre, a long-standing skate spot. Weekend food stalls behind the Royal Festival Hall are perfect for a bite to eat. It all adds up to a classic London afternoon, with your game as the warm-up.
